findings.title: Mobile topic-map h3 light-theme lightness changed from 20% to 50%
findings.body: The mobile `.topic-map h3` color was `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 20%)` and the diff rewrites it as `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%), ...)`. The primary-side lightness was silently changed from 20% to 50%, while the PR only intended to add the $secondary branch. In the default light theme, every mobile topic-map heading becomes much lighter than before. The desktop equivalent correctly keeps 20% and pairs it with 80% for $secondary, so the two platforms now also disagree.

findings.title: Mobile .custom-message-length light-theme color flipped from 70% to 30% lightness
findings.body: `.custom-message-length` previously used `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%)`, a faded light gray. The new value is `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 70%))`, so the light-theme branch now uses 30%. That is a much darker color than before for the character-count hint in mobile modals. The dark-theme pairing (70% of $secondary) was copied from the desktop file, but the primary-side value should have stayed at 70%. The desktop version of this rule is correct (70% / 30%).

findings.title: Embedded-post author link light-theme color changed from 30% to 70% lightness
findings.body: In `.embedded-posts .topic-meta-data h5 a`, the original color was `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)`, which is a dark, bold link color. The diff replaces it with `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 30%))`, so the light-theme link color jumps to 70% lightness. Links in embedded post headers become faint and lose contrast against the background in the default theme. The primary value should have remained 30%, with 70% as the $secondary counterpart.

findings.title: Desktop group-member .name light-theme lightness changed from 30% to 50%
findings.body: `.group-member-info .name` previously used `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)`. The diff changes the light-theme branch to `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%)` while also adding the $secondary branch. This is an unintended change to the light-theme value that the PR description does not mention. The name is noticeably lighter in the default theme and now differs from the 30% value used for the same name elsewhere.

findings.title: Mobile group-member .name light-theme lightness changed from 30% to 50%
findings.body: Same problem as the desktop file: `.group-member-info .name` previously used `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)`. The new `dark-light-choose` call uses `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%)` for the light theme, so the light-theme color changes without being intended. The $secondary branch should have been `scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 70%)` to mirror the original 30%, and the primary branch should have kept 30%.

findings.title: Comment says the topic-list cell default is a plain scale-color, which is no longer true
findings.body: The comment says the default color for table cells in the topic list is `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%)`. This PR changes the `td` and `th` defaults in `_topic-list.scss` to `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 50%))`. The comment now documents a value that is no longer the effective default, and it will mislead anyone tuning the coldmap colors.
